_demoProvenance: Entirely invented history for fictional Steve.

periods.d: Steve took photographs on his phone and went to local gigs. After a quieter spell, he returned to photography with a borrowed camera in the current year.

periods.n: Sunday dinners and a settled flat
periods.d: Ordinary dinners with friends became part of Steve's life. Moving to the new flat took longer to settle than he expected.

periods.n: Making Space for Health and Friends
periods.d: Steve is testing a week with room for exercise, photographs and friends. The work-free-evenings trial has started; its planned finish is still ahead.
Steve kept an notebook of drawings, questions and favourite days.
Steve wrote brief notes after walks, separating what happened from what he thought about it.
A small monthly group gave Steve a place to discuss changes and hear other perspectives.
Steve wrote about the new job, tired evenings and trying a smaller plan. His notes are selected observations, not causal evidence.
Steve learned layout and practical design in an entirely college course.
Steve worked at a local library and took an evening course in digital design.
Steve joined a small studio and learned to ask colleagues for early feedback.

periods.n: Designing services with a small team
periods.d: Steve worked with an team on ordinary service design projects.
Steve chose a new role and tried agreeing earlier finishes during its first fortnight.
A wholly family routine of pancakes, library visits and rainy-day board games.
Steve shared a small flat, learned two reliable dinners and divided the bills with his housemates.

periods.n: A flat with room for friends
periods.d: Steve made space for visitors and a small desk for photographs.
Steve, Maya and Leo met for games, taking turns to host. Steve hosted the August evening in his new flat.
Steve and Maya tried a regular walk, keeping the route short when either was tired.
Steve built model aircraft, painted them badly at first and enjoyed making small things.
An school band practised in a garage and played two local evenings.
Steve read short novels with a local group and sometimes went along without finishing.
Steve practised framing on familiar walks and shared three imperfect photographs.
Steve tried push, pull and legs sessions, then shortened one workout during the new job.

events.d: Steve noticed that movement and sleep were easier to understand across weeks than on a single bad day.
Steve tried one push, one pull, and one legs session.
Steve found two meals he would happily repeat.
Steve listed his recurring bills and found one subscription he no longer used.
Maya, Leo, and Steve met for an ordinary evening together.
Steve practised framing during a walk and saved three photos he liked.
Steve started the role he wanted and met his new team. There was a lot to learn on the first day.
Agreed two work-free evenings and a clear handover for a four-week trial. The agreement is ready to try in the following week.
Steve shared three photographs before trying to make them perfect. The same moment is recorded in his Journal and Artist evidence.
Steve tried a twenty-minute workout after a busy day.
Steve showed his invented notebook to the school art group.
The fictional band played three songs for friends and families.
Steve completed an invented final project about finding a local library.

events.n: First dinner in the painted room
events.d: Steve invited Maya and Leo for an easy dinner after painting the spare room.
Steve listened during an invented group conversation and wrote down one question to return to.

events.n: Borrowed a camera for the canal walk
events.d: Steve returned to photography, borrowing a camera and trying two views of the same bridge.

events.n: Read an unfinished book with the group
events.d: Steve went to book club after reading only half the novel and enjoyed the conversation.
Steve and Maya chose a short walk and a warm drink instead of cancelling.
Steve asked his manager about two work-free evenings and discussed what a clear handover would need.

events.n: One question at the end of the week
events.d: Steve wrote: What felt spacious this week? This invented line is a question, not a score.
